I don't know the exact measurements of the ingredients but I believe the =ecipe goes something like this... 
Select long thin eggplants that feel light. (You don't want =eeds) 
Remove stems and tips and cut them lengthwise in thin slices —'/. inch =hick 
Salt each slice lightly on both sides, place them on paper towels to =rain. 
Put a heavy weight on top of the sliced layers of eggplant and let stand in refrigerator, preferably overnight. 
Next day remove eggplant and allow to reach room =emperature. 
Simultaneously heat about 1 inch of vegetable oil in deep frying pan and do the following: 
Beat 6 eggs in bowl. 
Place=Wondra flour on a plate. Dip each slice in the beaten eggs and let drip free of eggs. Dredge in flour. Shake 
excess off. 
Oil has to be very hot about 350 degrees or the eggplant will get soggy =nstead of crispy. 
Place=eggplant slices into oil. Make sure to use a spatula because a fork will =rick the eggplant and allow the oil 
to seep in. Turn slices over when one =ide is golden and the eggplant appears stiff. Remove when both sides are =olden. 
Drain oil from eggplant by placing on paper towels. 
Allow=eggplant to cool down. Add tomato sauce to each piece of eggplant so it gets absorbed. 
Mix ricotta cheese, mozzarella, eggs, grated cheese (Locatelli) a little =alt and black pepper into a =ig bowl. 
Make the mixture somewhat firm. Put a thin coat of the cheese mixture on each =lice.
